- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.2) and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast slope to avoid underreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast slope for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline after peak), model often fails to recognize — adjust forecast to reflect gradual decline.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0) and forecast is flat, check for lag — if true outcome diverges, increase forecast sensitivity to recent history.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if model consistently underestimates true outcome by 5–10% in early days, increase initial forecast value by 2–3% to account for momentum.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated small positive spikes (e.g., 0.20) followed by large negative moves, model often fails to anticipate — add a 1–2 day lag correction to forecast.
